summary: The prepared source already contained the validated Mooncake index-batching implementation from sgl-project/sglang#32758, but its default remained 0 (disabled). Therefore the original command, which does not set SGLANG_MOONCAKE_MAX_TRANSFER_BATCH_INDICES, still used one unbounded synchronous all-layer transfer. Changed the default to the issue-specific validated value of 1024 while retaining explicit 0 as the legacy escape hatch, and added a regression for the real default.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before check: the recorded base did not enable the validated 1024-index bound by default.

6 tests and 3 subtests passed: configured default, ordered long-transfer slicing, exact/under-boundary legacy fast path, explicit 0 behavior, failure short-circuiting, device-page indices, and unchanged custom-memory-pool behavior.
40 related disaggregation status, timeout, failure-cleanup, queue-cleanup, and deferred-release tests passed.

tests.command: environment default/override assertions using the prepared interpreter
tests.what_was_measured: Observed default=1024, explicit disabled value=0, and explicit override=2048.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned device was inspected as one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The corrected behavior is CPU-side construction and submission of Mooncake address batches; no relevant Mooncake multi-node transport fixture, GLM-5.2 weights, NVIDIA H100s, or the reported 2-node prefill/4-node decode topology were available. No unrelated GPU smoke is claimed as validation.

remaining_limitations: The original intermittent deployment was not reproduced end-to-end because GLM-5.2 weights, NVIDIA H100 hardware, Mooncake/RDMA peers, and the reported multi-node topology were unavailable.

The issue-specific upstream validation used GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on separate 4x L20D prefill and decode nodes with an approximately 800K-token workload; this task independently verified the prepared implementation and its batching boundaries, not that full deployment.
The source issue reports GLM-5.2 with DSA/HiCache/HiSparse and a different topology, so model-architecture semantics and distributed behavior remain unverified here.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
